steps.body: The pattern extends one more step: **angles all the way around a single point total 360°** — a full turn. Three known angles: 100°, 120°, and 90° sum to 310°; the missing fourth angle is 360−310=**50°.**
Turn past a straight angle to create a reflex angle.

widget.prompt: Turn the point counterclockwise through 270°. Watch the turn pass 180° before it stops.

commonTurns.feedback: 180° is a straight angle. Keep turning another quarter-turn to reach 270°.
90° is only one quarter-turn. A reflex angle must pass 180°.

widget.successFeedback: 270° is three quarter-turns. It is greater than 180°, so it is a reflex angle.
widget.lowFeedback: The turn has not reached 270° yet. Keep moving counterclockwise.
widget.highFeedback: The turn has passed 270°. Move back one step.

predict.prompt: Can a single angle around a point measure MORE than 180°?
predict.reveal: A full turn is 360°, and one angle can claim most of it — a 200° angle wraps well past straight. Around-a-point problems welcome the big ones.

explanationVariants: Adding the three knowns, then subtracting from 360.

widget.prompt: Four angles surround a point. Three are 100°, 120°, and 90°. What is the fourth?

commonErrors.feedback: 310 is just the sum of the three knowns — not the missing angle yet. Subtract it from 360: 50.
130 subtracts from 180 instead of the full-turn total. All the way around a point is 360: 360−310=50.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Add the three known angles, then subtract from 360.

steps.body: Three benchmarks, one toolkit: a **right angle** totals 90°, a **straight line** totals 180°, and **all the way around a point** totals 360°. Reading the figure's description tells you which one applies.

explanationVariants: 'All the way around a point' is the full-turn benchmark: 360°.
The description names the total directly.

widget.prompt: A figure describes angles going 'all the way around a single point.' What do they total?

options.feedback: A full turn around a point always totals 360°.
180° is the straight-line benchmark, not a full turn. Around a point is 360°.
90° is the right-angle benchmark, far short of a full turn. Around a point is 360°.

options.label: It depends on how many angles there are
options.feedback: The TOTAL stays 360° regardless of how many angles split it — only the individual pieces change.

widget.prompt: Match each figure description to its total.

left.label: A right angle split into parts
Angles all the way around a point

pairErrors.feedback: 360° belongs to a full turn around a point. A right angle split into parts still totals 90°.

widget.missFeedback: Line=180°, right angle=90°, full turn around a point=360°.
widget.successFeedback: Three different figures, three different totals — the description names which one applies.

explanationVariants: Add the three knowns, then subtract from 360.

widget.prompt: Four angles surround a point. Three are 150°, 80°, and 60°. What is the fourth?

commonErrors.feedback: 290 is just the sum of the three knowns — not the missing angle yet. Subtract it from 360: 70.
10 subtracts the knowns from each other instead of adding them first. Add all three (150+80+60=290), then subtract from 360: 70.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Add the three known angles, then subtract that total from 360.

hints: The wheel's spokes create angles all the way around its center — a full turn.
Add the three known spoke angles: 85+95+110.
Subtract that total from 360 for the last spoke angle.
explanationVariants: Adding the three known spoke angles, then subtracting from 360, gives the missing one.

widget.prompt: A wheel has 4 spokes creating 4 angles around its center. Three of the angles are 85°, 95°, and 110°. What is the fourth angle?

commonErrors.feedback: 290 is just the sum of the three known spoke angles — not the missing one yet. Subtract it from 360: 70.
180 uses the straight-line benchmark — but spokes around a wheel's center make a full turn, 360°: 360−290=70.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Add the three known angles, then subtract that total from 360.

takeaways: A full turn around a single point always totals 360°.
Right angle (90°), straight line (180°), and full turn (360°) form one benchmark toolkit.
With several angles, add every known one first, then subtract from the right total.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **A full turn around a point totals 360°.** With three angles known — say 90°, 90°, and 90° — they sum to 270°, so the last one is 360−270=90°.

explanationVariants: Adding the three knowns, then subtracting from 360.

widget.prompt: Four angles surround a point. Three are each 90°. What is the fourth?

options.feedback: 270 is just the sum of the three knowns. Subtract it from 360: 90.
That uses the straight-line total instead of the full-turn total. Around a point is 360: 360−270=90.
